newsitem.title: USA: Study says infant flat-headedness can be corrected.
newsitem.headline: Study says infant flat-headedness can be corrected.

text.p: Most infants who develop flat-headedness in the early months of life do not need surgery to correct the problem, U.S. researchers said on Monday.
If the back or side of the head becomes misshapen, a change in sleeping position or use of a helmet can correct the problem, the report from Children's Hospital in Pittsburgh said.

Researchers said they studied 71 children with the condition and found 69 of them could be treated simply by alternating head positions during sleep. The other two cases involved a premature closure of the skull's growth sites that would require surgery, they said.
The report was published in this month's issue of Pediatrics, a journal from the American Academy of Pediatrics.
The issue has stirred interest because doctors now recommend that children be put to sleep on their backs to lower the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome.

In view of that, the report said, "it is apparent that parents must be carefully instructed to alternate (head) positioning from one side to the other" during sleep to avoid flattening one side or the back of the infant's head.
The academy advised parents to put babies to sleep on their backs "while making sure the infants get plenty of 'tummy time' when awake."
